pixel art sprite.constraints: Draw it as a chunky 16-bit video game sprite on a coarse, clearly visible pixel grid, about sixty pixels across the whole subject, every pixel a hard-edged square of one flat color. No anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no smooth shading, no glossy highlights and no noisy dithering: shade with only two or three flat steps of each color, laid down as solid clusters of square pixels. Keep to a small limited palette taken from the brand colors below, plus cream and warm brown only where an animal's own coloring needs them. Outline every shape with a darker step of its own color, never with black, and never fill a large area with black or grey. Build the subject from a few big parts, large and centered, never from a heap of small pieces. Leave the background fully empty and transparent behind, around and beneath the subject: no backdrop, no floor, no ground shadow, no frame, no border, no glow and no vignette, so the whole sprite lifts off the page in one piece.
